resources.string: AutoSkip will tap “Skip ad” as soon as it appears in YouTube.
The service is installed, but you have paused AutoSkip.
Turn on AutoSkip in Accessibility settings so it can work.
AutoSkip has no internet access. It doesn\'t collect, store or send any data: it only looks for the “Skip ad” button inside YouTube.
AutoSkip is free, open source and non-profit. Donations help us improve the organization.
AutoSkip needs the Accessibility permission to detect the “Skip ad” button while you watch videos on YouTube and tap it for you.
• Reads the screen only while YouTube is open.\n• Looks only for the “Skip ad” button (in any language).\n• When the button is visible and tappable, taps it once.
• Never taps anything else: no videos, comments, likes, subscriptions or searches.\n• Doesn\'t read other apps, messages or passwords.\n• Has no internet access and doesn\'t send or store data.

1. Tap “Open Accessibility settings”.
2. Go to “Installed apps” or “Downloaded services”.
3. Choose “AutoSkip” and turn it on.
4. Confirm the system prompt.

Seeing “Restricted setting” and can\'t turn it on? This happens on Android 13+ when the app isn\'t installed from the Play Store. Open App info, tap ⋮ (top right) → “Allow restricted settings”, then try again.
AutoSkip detects the “Skip ad” button in the YouTube app and taps it automatically. It only reads YouTube\'s screen, never taps anything else, and doesn\'t collect or send any data.
